extra_misconceptions.fact: Intact skin over a blister acts as a sterile barrier against bacteria, so leave small blisters unbroken and pad them with moleskin.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Popping a friction blister with an unsterilized pin right before the run segment speeds up skin healing.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Heatstroke victims may have an altered mental state and choke on fluids, so focus on rapid external cooling and call emergency services.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Drinking plain water as fast as possible is the safest treatment for an athlete showing confusion from heatstroke.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Exercise-associated cramps stem from neuromuscular fatigue and electrolyte loss, requiring reduced pace, gentle stretching, and sodium intake.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Muscle cramps during a long bike leg are caused strictly by lactic acid buildup and require immediate static stretching.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Water conducts heat away from the body roughly twenty-five times faster than air, causing hypothermia even in mild weather.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Hypothermia only threatens multisport athletes when the ambient air temperature drops below fifty degrees Fahrenheit.

extra_socratic_questions: Which physical indicator distinguishes life-threatening heatstroke from heat exhaustion during a hot run segment?
Why is it dangerous to apply ice directly to bare skin when treating an acute ankle sprain on the trail?
What happens to a swimmer's core body temperature and motor control when open-water hypothermia begins?
Under what condition does road rash from a cycling slide require professional medical evaluation for infection?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Annual exams screen for silent cardiovascular conditions, growth-related musculoskeletal changes, and updated immunization needs.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: An annual pre-participation physical exam is unnecessary if an athlete feels healthy and completed a race last season.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Fats and fiber slow gastric emptying and cause gastrointestinal distress during exercise, whereas easily digested carbohydrates fuel muscles.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Eating a heavy high-fat and high-fiber meal thirty minutes before a race maximizes available energy for the swim.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Decongestants and certain allergy medications can elevate heart rate, raise blood pressure, or impair thermoregulation during intense heat.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Over-the-counter antihistamines and decongestants do not need to be reported to a doctor during a sports exam.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Cycling crashes and barefoot transition runs expose skin to soil and pavement bacteria, making up-to-date tetanus protection essential.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Tetanus immunization status only matters for wilderness camping and has no relevance to paved multisport events.

extra_socratic_questions: Why is it dangerous to withhold a history of exercise-induced asthma or food allergies during a sports physical?
What happens to glycogen stores and endurance performance when an athlete trains daily without adequate sleep?
Which physical indicator in morning urine color confirms that an athlete is properly hydrated before training?
Under what condition does a family history of sudden cardiac issues change how a physician clears a youth athlete?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Standard triathlons always follow the strict swim-bike-run sequence so athletes complete the aquatic segment while freshest and safest.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: A standard triathlon allows competitors to complete the swim, bike, and run legs in any order they prefer.

extra_misconceptions.fact: A duathlon replaces the swim with an opening run, following a run-bike-run format, whereas an aquabike pairs swimming with cycling.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Duathlon events consist of a swimming leg followed by a cycling leg with no running segment required.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Targeted technical practice in your weakest event yields larger time savings and reduces fatigue carried into subsequent segments.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Spending all training time on your strongest discipline is the fastest way to lower your overall multisport finish time.

extra_misconceptions.fact: The cycling leg covers the longest distance and largest time proportion in most triathlons, followed by the run and then the swim.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: The swim segment accounts for the largest share of total distance and elapsed time in a standard triathlon.

extra_socratic_questions: Why is it dangerous to place the open-water swim leg at the end of a triathlon when athletes are most exhausted?
What distinguishes the segment sequence of a standard duathlon from an aquathlon or an aquabike event?
What happens to a triathlete's running stride and cadence during the first half-mile immediately after biking?
Which training measurement helps an athlete identify whether swimming, biking, or running is their weakest discipline?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Bicycles operate as vehicles and must ride with the flow of traffic on the right, while pedestrians run facing oncoming traffic.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Cyclists and runners share the exact same road rule and should both travel facing oncoming vehicular traffic.

extra_misconceptions.fact: A helmet must sit level just two finger-widths above the eyebrows so the foam shell absorbs frontal impact forces in a forward fall.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: A bicycle helmet worn tilted back to expose the forehead still provides full impact protection during a crash.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Open water introduces currents, cold shock, and limited visibility, requiring all eight points of Safe Swim Defense and active lifeguards.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Pool swimming skill guarantees safe open-water performance without needing lookouts or a designated buddy system.

extra_misconceptions.fact: A full pre-ride check requires verifying tire sidewall pressure, spinning both wheels for clearance, and testing front and rear brakes.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Squeezing one brake lever halfway to the handlebar confirms both brakes and tires are ready for a race course.

extra_socratic_questions: What measurement confirms that a cycling helmet chin strap and brow pad are adjusted to protect the forehead?
Which three mechanical components must a Scout inspect during an ABC Quick Check before wheeling a bike to transition?
Where should a Scout position themselves relative to oncoming traffic when running on a road without sidewalks?
Under what condition does Scouting America Safe Swim Defense require suspending an open-water swim session immediately?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Dynamic warmup movements increase blood flow and tissue temperature before exercise, while static stretching belongs in the cooldown.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Holding deep static stretches for sixty seconds on cold muscles is the safest way to start a training session.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Gradual progression paired with recovery days allows physiological adaptation and prevents overuse injuries like shin splints or tendinitis.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Doubling training volume and intensity every three days builds cardiovascular endurance twice as fast over four weeks.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Brick workouts that transition immediately from cycling to running train the nervous system to adapt to shifting muscle recruitment patterns.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Training each sport only on separate days prepares the legs completely for the feeling of running off the bike.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Each logged training session must last at least twenty-five minutes and include both a pre-workout warmup and post-workout stretching.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: A workout session shorter than twenty-five minutes without a cooldown still satisfies the four-week conditioning plan.

extra_socratic_questions: What happens to cold muscle fibers and connective tissue when an athlete performs aggressive static stretches before warming up?
Why is it beneficial to schedule a combined bike-to-run brick workout during a four-week multisport conditioning plan?
What workout log details beyond total minutes help you and your counselor evaluate progressive endurance gains?
Under what condition should an athlete replace a scheduled high-intensity session with active recovery or rest?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Riders must walk or run alongside their bikes inside the transition zone and mount only after crossing the designated mount line.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Athletes save time by riding their bicycles directly from the transition rack out through the pedestrian chute.

extra_misconceptions.fact: The helmet chin strap must remain securely fastened before taking the bike off the rack and until the bike is re-racked after the ride.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Unbuckling the helmet strap while coasting toward the dismount line is allowed as long as the helmet stays on.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Transition footprints must stay compact on a folded towel immediately beside your wheel so you do not block neighboring athletes.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Spreading gear across three feet of space next to your bike rack makes items easier to grab during transition.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Racking the bike in a moderate-to-easy gear lets tired legs spin smoothly from a standing start without straining knees or dropping chains.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Leaving the bicycle in its hardest high gear at the rack makes accelerating past the mount line much easier.

extra_socratic_questions: Why is it a safety violation to unbuckle your helmet chin strap before placing your bike back on the transition rack?
Where should a Scout position their running shoes, helmet, and race belt on the transition towel to prevent tangling?
What happens to rider balance and surrounding athletes if a cyclist attempts to mount before crossing the mount line?
Which gear setup choice makes pulling on running shoes faster when transitioning with wet or tired feet?

extra_misconceptions.fact: All segments of the chosen multisport event must be completed consecutively on the same day with smooth, safe transitions between each leg.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Completing the swim in the morning and finishing the bike and run segments that evening satisfies requirement seven.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Running with a quick, controlled cadence for the first few hundred meters lets blood flow redistribute from cycling to running muscles.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Starting the final one-kilometer run at an all-out sprint immediately out of transition prevents leg stiffness.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Walking the transition entry, rack position, and exit chutes before starting prevents wrong turns and collisions when heart rate is high.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: An event-day walkthrough of the transition area is unnecessary if you practiced setting up your gear the week before.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Keeping eyes focused several yards ahead down the course allows early hazard detection, smoother cornering, and safe passing distance.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Looking straight down at the front tire while cycling helps an athlete maintain a straighter line on the course.

extra_socratic_questions: What happens to your bike and run splits if you sprint the opening hundred-meter swim at maximum anaerobic effort?
Which shifting technique before stopping at the dismount line prepares your bike for a clean stop and smooth transition?
What measurement confirms that you completed all required segments consecutively on the same day for your chosen option?
Under what condition should an athlete slow their pace or alert a course marshal during the culminating multisport event?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Beginner and youth multisport events welcome road, hybrid, or mountain bikes provided they pass a basic mechanical safety inspection.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Youth athletes must own an expensive carbon-fiber time-trial bicycle to enter a sanctioned community triathlon.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Paratriathletes race all three segments using adaptive equipment such as tandem bicycles, handcycles, racing wheelchairs, or prosthetics.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Paralympic triathletes only compete in single-sport exhibition races rather than full swim-bike-run courses.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Observing hundreds of athletes navigate transition and aid stations reveals common gear mistakes and pacing strategies firsthand.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Volunteering at a local multisport event offers no value toward improving your own race execution and transition skills.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Local park districts, youth clubs, and sprint-distance races offer accessible, age-appropriate multisport events close to home.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Multisport participation after earning this merit badge requires traveling to full-distance Ironman competitions.

extra_socratic_questions: What role do sighted guides and specialized handcycles play in enabling Paralympic athletes to compete in triathlon?
Which responsibilities at a local race aid station or transition area teach a Scout volunteer how events operate safely?
What happens to long-term training consistency when an athlete joins a local youth triathlon club or school swim team?
Where can a youth athlete verify age-group distance standards and sanctioning rules for community multisport races?
